issues.legal_issue: A renewed lease that incorporates the original lease covenants without reservation may preserve an unexhausted option to renew, while the resulting further lease need not itself provide another renewal option.
material_facts: The original lease contained an option to renew for a further term.
The first renewal was executed in a fresh deed that incorporated all covenants and stipulations of the original lease without reservation.
The lessee exercised the option for another renewal, and the State’s officials had recommended or supported renewal before the State disputed the entitlement.
The State had not exercised a right of re-entry before the lessee exercised the renewal option.
issues.conclusion: The lessee was entitled to a further 50-year renewal commencing May 20, 1987. The lease granted for that term need not include a further renewal covenant, so the ruling does not create a right to successive renewals under that new lease.
issues.legal_principle: Whether a renewal covenant carries into a renewed lease depends on the language of the original covenant, the renewed deed, the parties’ intention and the surrounding circumstances, read as a whole. A renewal requires a fresh lease deed. Although the law does not prohibit a perpetual lease, courts lean against perpetual renewal and generally require clear and unambiguous language to establish it. The Court agreed with Syed Jaleel Zane v. P. Venkata Murlidhar & Ors. and Secretary of State for India in Council v. A.H. Forbes; it also relied on Green v. Palmer and referred to Baker v. Merckel and Mulla on the Transfer of Property Act. The principle in Green v. Palmer supports including a renewal covenant in the renewed lease where the original language requires it, without thereby creating an endless succession of renewals.

rule.if: lease_renewal_appeal and original_lease_allowed_renewal and first_renewal_incorporated_original_covenants_without_reservation and lessee_exercised_further_option

predicates.lease_renewal_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning a lessee’s claimed right to renew a lease.
predicates.original_lease_allowed_renewal: The original lease gave the lessee an option to renew.
predicates.first_renewal_incorporated_original_cove: The deed for the first renewal incorporated the original lease’s covenants without reserving an exception for the renewal covenant.
predicates.lessee_exercised_further_option: The lessee exercised the claimed option for a further renewal.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns a further lease renewal, the original lease provided an option, the first renewal carried forward the original covenants without reservation, and the lessee exercised the further option, the further renewal is granted without providing another option in the new lease.

issues.legal_issue: A government cannot rely on a purported acquisition of land it already owns to prevent renewal of a lease over that land.
material_facts: The land’s ownership vested in the State, while the respondent held a leasehold interest.
The State issued acquisition notifications concerning the land beneath the bungalow, but did not seek to acquire the leasehold rights or the superstructure.
The State relied on those notifications as a reason renewal could not proceed.
issues.conclusion: The acquisition notifications did not prevent renewal of the lease and were to be ignored for that purpose.
issues.legal_principle: The Land Acquisition Act, 1894 cannot be invoked by the Government to acquire its own property. A purported acquisition of land already owned by the State does not prevent lease renewal where the State has not proposed to acquire the leasehold rights or the superstructure. The Court relied on Sharda Devi v. State of Bihar and addressed the notifications under Sections 4 and 6 of the Act.

predicates.lease_renewal_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning renewal of a lease.
predicates.land_already_owned_by_government: The government already owns the land subject to the lease.
predicates.acquisition_targeted_land_not_leasehold_: The government’s purported acquisition concerned the land itself and did not seek to acquire the leasehold rights or the superstructure.

issues.definition: In an appeal concerning lease renewal, a purported acquisition does not prevent renewal when the government already owns the land and the acquisition does not target the leasehold rights or the superstructure.

issues.legal_issue: An alleged lease breach does not stall exercise of a renewal option when the alleged breach is unsubstantiated or the lessor has not acted on its re-entry right before the option is exercised.
material_facts: The State alleged that the lessee was negotiating a sale in breach of the lease, but the High Court found that allegation unsubstantiated.
The State had not taken steps to exercise its right of re-entry before the lessee exercised the renewal option.
The State argued that the alleged breach made the lessee ineligible for renewal.
issues.conclusion: The alleged breach did not prevent the lessee from exercising the renewal option. Any right of re-entry available to the lessor could be exercised separately, without regard to renewal.
issues.legal_principle: An unsubstantiated allegation of breach cannot defeat renewal. Even where a lease gives the lessor a right of re-entry for breach, a proposed exercise of that right does not stall an already exercised renewal option when no steps to re-enter were taken before the option was exercised; the right of re-entry remains separately available.

rule.if: lease_renewal_appeal and lessee_exercised_renewal_option and (alleged_breach_unsubstantiated or reentry_not_started_before_option)

predicates.lease_renewal_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning a lessee’s exercise of a lease renewal option.
predicates.lessee_exercised_renewal_option: The lessee exercised the option to renew the lease.
predicates.alleged_breach_unsubstantiated: The lessor alleged a lease breach, but the allegation was not substantiated.
predicates.reentry_not_started_before_option: The lessor had not taken steps to exercise its right of re-entry before the lessee exercised the renewal option.

issues.definition: In an appeal concerning a renewal option, an alleged breach does not stall the option’s exercise when the lessee exercised it and the allegation was unsubstantiated or the lessor had not begun re-entry beforehand.
